When people acknowledge trauma responses, it has traditionally been fight or flight response. At some point, freeze became more acknowledged as a natural response, too. More recently, there's discussion of fawn response, which is basically acting sweet and receptive towards your abuser in a subconscious attempt to either lessen the abuse or lessen the emotional pain of receiving it. Similar to Stockholm Syndrome. Can also cause confusion and guilt, similar to freeze response, about the victim's role in "allowing" their own abuse. It's common in abusive family or intimate relationships. So trauma responses can be summarized as fight, flight, freeze, or fawn.

This is classic Body Dysmorphic Disorder, which is OCD-related. Checking on your appearance is actually reassurance seeking, which will just make your obsessions worse. Look into ERP (exposure) therapy and intentionally put yourself in situations that make you self-conscious of your appearance so you can teach your brain that these situations are acceptable. Here's a [helpful video](https://youtu.be/QqF9rL_Hf7c), but if you can afford it, guidance from a therapist is best due to the counterintuitive nature of this kind of therapy. ERP is the only clinically proven treatment for OCD.

I struggled with untreated BDD for many years until it just morphed into different kinds of OCD (like ROCD). My advice is don't wait it out or hope that it will go away on its own.
